primitives.name: DFS Optimal Solution Oracle
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Python lane used by the DFS oracle only (dev-time verification, never shipped).
primitives.latex:
maximize \; score(S) = \sum_{i \in S} p_i x_i 
subject to \; budget \le B, \; x_i \in \{0,1\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'Set of selected players (dimensionless)', 'p_i': 'Player fantasy points (points)', 'x_i': 'Binary selection indicator (dimensionless)', 'B': 'Salary budget (dollars)'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) Player scores are known (2) Budget is fixed (3) Only one player per position.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exponential search space O(2^n) for n candidates.

layer2.mapping: Serves as ground truth for GSI out-of-sample performance testing and GSE policy evaluation.
layer2.telemetry: Oracle optimality gap quantifies engine suboptimality.

This structure creates a rigorous duality between exact optimization (GSI) and heuristic search (GSE), with the oracle acting as a shared reference point. Failure occurs when solver timeouts exceed deployment latency thresholds, necessitating approximate methods.
